audit.whatIsWrong: The level chart contradicted the data twice over. Akali wins 57.04% across 696 games, yet the content layer gave Cassiopeia 5 of 7 stages; and the two layers disagreed on six of seven rows (phases[].side read Skill/Skill/Skill/Skill/Akali/Skill/Skill while win[] read Cassiopeia x4, Akali, Cassiopeia, Akali).
audit.why: Cassiopeia genuinely owns levels 1-2 on range (Noxious Blast 850 vs Akali's 550 Q) and on Miasma's 24-second level-1 grounding. From level 3 the shroud denies targeted Twin Fang, and from 4-5 Akali's E (11.5s) cycles faster than Miasma (18s), so the lane tilts. That shape matches a 57% win rate; the old chart did not.
audit.corrected: Whole chart reproposed in matched pairs, both layers: Cassiopeia, Cassiopeia, Skill, Akali, Akali, Akali, Akali, with ratings 4/4/5/6/7/6/7 and rewritten whys.

audit.whatIsWrong: Spike text used the fabricated name 'Noxious Blight' and 'Petrify', and never named Cassiopeia's real spike (Miasma's cooldown falling from 24s to 16s) or Akali's (Grievous Wounds cancelling Twin Fang sustain at first item).
audit.why: Riot's names are Noxious Blast (Q) and Petrifying Gaze (R). Cassiopeia's power in this lane is entirely Miasma uptime; Akali's answer is the gap between Miasma casts, which widens as her E cooldown drops to 10s.
audit.corrected: spikes[0].text, spikes[1].text and the level-6 / first-item whys rewritten around real names and real cooldowns.

audit.whatIsWrong: Three decisive interactions were absent. (a) Miasma grounds — that kills Akali's E RE-CAST mid-flip and BOTH casts of Perfect Execution, not just 'dashes and leaps' generically. (b) Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing Cassiopeia; a target with its back turned is merely slowed, so a flank entry defuses her ultimate. (c) Twin Fang heals her for a percentage of damage dealt and deals bonus damage to poisoned targets — Grievous Wounds is a matchup item, not a generic note.
audit.why: All three are stated in Riot's own descriptions in the kit file. The flagged missing-interaction rule 'needs-antiheal' names Twin Fang explicitly.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, dontsFull[1].d, breakdown.carry, enemyWin, report[8].t, early and spikes[1].text rewritten to state all three.

audit.whatIsWrong: No cooldown numbers anywhere. Twin Fang was implicitly treated as a punishable spell.
audit.why: Twin Fang is a 0.75s cooldown — it can never be baited out. Miasma (24/22/20/18/16) is the only punishable cooldown in the kit; Petrifying Gaze is 120/100/80.
audit.corrected: breakdown.cooldowns now names Miasma's 24s-to-16s band as the lane's clock and tells the player to buy Grievous Wounds instead of waiting on Twin Fang.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Add anti-heal early into his sustain' — vague, wrong pronoun, and no source named.
audit.why: The sustain is Twin Fang specifically.
audit.corrected: report[8].t now names Grievous Wounds against Twin Fang.

edits.before: Q the wave edge and his toes — the energy crunch is real, so every kama needs to farm AND poke at once.
edits.after: Noxious Blast reaches 850 to your 550 and she gets it back every 3.5s — farm the back of the wave, do not contest.

edits.before: More Q pressure — hold the energy bar above 100 so a real trade window never finds you broke.
edits.after: Miasma is 24s at rank 1, her longest cooldown of the game — while it is up, no step forward is worth it.

edits.before: Shroud online: the trade pattern is Q-auto, shroud the answer, Q again from the smoke. Most mids lose this exchange.
edits.after: Shroud online — she cannot target Twin Fang into the smoke, but Noxious Blast still lands on the zone. Even trades.

edits.before: Passive-weave every trade: spell, walk out of the ring, auto the edge — the energy refunds pay the whole lane.
edits.after: Miasma is her only answer to your E, and it is down 16s at rank 5 — that gap is where your passive-weave trades live.

edits.before: Perfect Execution online — the double-dash R turns half-health mages into clean-up duty. Look for the all-in.
edits.after: Perfect Execution online — she has no dash, so once Miasma is spent the double-dash R is a clean kill on a poked Cass.

edits.before: First item spike: shroud trades become kill threats. Force the wave contact and punish every spell he whiffs.
edits.after: First item plus Grievous Wounds: her Twin Fang healing stops paying, and one shrouded window becomes a kill.

edits.before: Late Akali erases carries: R in through the front line, shroud the response, E-reset out with the kill.
edits.after: Flank her: Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing her, so enter from behind and she gets a slow, not a stun.

edits.before: Cassiopeia: at level 1 her poison and range already out-trade Akali's short-range poke.
edits.after: Cassiopeia: Noxious Blast reaches 850 on a 3.5s cooldown against Akali's 550 Q.

edits.before: Cassiopeia: level 2 gives her more zone control from Noxious Blight that Akali can't contest yet.
edits.after: Cassiopeia: Miasma at level 2 grounds Akali's E flip for its full duration, and it is up every 24s.

edits.before: Cassiopeia: level 3 widens her range/DPS advantage before Akali's kit is fully online.
edits.after: Skill: Twilight Shroud denies targeted Twin Fang, but Noxious Blast still hits the smoke.

edits.before: Cassiopeia: levels 4-5 let her poke freely since Akali still lacks the burst to punish approaches.
edits.after: Akali: Miasma drops to 18 seconds but Akali's E is 11.5 — she can flip in on every Miasma gap.

edits.before: Akali: level 6 grants Akali a genuine engage window through stealth and dash-execute that offsets Petrify.
edits.after: Akali: level 6 stealth plus the dash-execute beats Petrifying Gaze, which only stuns targets facing her.

edits.before: Cassiopeia: first item Rylai's/Liandry's still lets her out-damage Akali in a straight poke war.
edits.after: Akali: first item plus Grievous Wounds shuts off Twin Fang's healing, and one shrouded window kills.

edits.before: Akali: with a full burst item late, Akali can flank and delete Cassiopeia before Petrify lands.
edits.after: Akali: flank from behind and Petrifying Gaze only slows — she has no dash to survive the R reset.

edits.before: - Cassiopeia Miasma: matchup-defining — Grounds you — dashes and leaps are disabled inside it. Check it before every step-up. - W Twilight Shroud is the lifeline; chip damage never gets it. - The ult answers fights, not waves.
edits.after: - Cassiopeia Miasma: it grounds you — E-recast and both R dashes die inside it. 24s at rank 1, 16s at rank 5, and that gap is the lane. - Twin Fang is 0.75s: never plan around it, buy Grievous Wounds. - Petrifying Gaze only stuns you facing her.

edits.before: Grounds you — dashes and leaps are disabled inside it. Commit on its cooldown, never into it.
edits.after: It grounds you: E-recast and both R dashes die inside it. Commit in the 16-24s gap, never into it.

edits.before: Cassiopeia whiffs Miasma and the lane briefly belongs to you.
edits.after: Miasma spent on nothing is a 16-second door — walk through it now.

edits.before: That is Cassiopeia’s rehearsed moment — don’t audition for it.
edits.after: Shroud is your only exit from a Miasma-grounded all-in — keep it.

edits.before: The shroud spent farming is the dive you can't answer — W is your Flash, your Zhonya's, and your opening all at once.
edits.after: Noxious Blast outranges your Q by 300 and Twin Fang heals her back — you lose every pre-3 exchange on math alone.

edits.before: Carry through deletions — one carry per fight, every fight; the shroud buys the time and the resets pay the exit.
edits.after: Cassiopeia is the deletion target — enter behind her so Petrifying Gaze only slows, then R, shroud, E-reset out.

edits.before: If Cassiopeia opens the score, reset expectations and respect Miasma doubly. After a second, your job description changes — farm with Q range and stay relevant through shroud picks.
edits.after: If Cassiopeia opens the score, never cross her Miasma line — grounded, you cannot leave. Farm at Q range, buy Grievous Wounds early, and stay relevant through shroud picks.

edits.before: Cassiopeia wins by landing Miasma, denying your pattern, and owning the spacing war until your tempo starves.
edits.after: Cassiopeia wins by grounding you in Miasma, healing the trade back with Twin Fang, and stunning you as you face her.

edits.before: Start Doran's Shield or Ring + pots. Riftmaker or Stormsurge-line first, Sorcerer's/Mercs, then Zhonya's into burst, Rabadon's after. Add anti-heal early into his sustain.
edits.after: Start Doran's Shield or Ring + pots. Riftmaker or Stormsurge-line first, Sorcerer's/Mercs, then Zhonya's into burst, Rabadon's after. Grievous Wounds early — Twin Fang heals her.

edits.before: Cassiopeia's Noxious Blight-Twin Fang combo melts your HP bar in one rotation if you sit in her E zone, and she outranges your Q from level 3 on.
edits.after: Cassiopeia's Noxious Blast into Twin Fang melts you in one rotation if you stand in the poison, and Twin Fang heals her back for the whole trade.

edits.before: Petrify's stun still threatens to lock you down, but your R gives you the burst window to punish her the moment she misses it.
edits.after: Petrifying Gaze only stuns enemies facing her, so R past her and it becomes a slow — then the double-dash punishes the whiff.

edits.before: Cassiopeia out-ranges you badly with Noxious Blight and her passive movement speed lets her kite your E flip. Avoid standing in her poison cloud since Twin Fang execute damage scales with it, and never dash in without seeing where Petrify is coming from — the stun into full combo can nearly half your HP. Play patient, farm with Q from max range, and wait for level 6 before considering any real trade.
edits.after: Cassiopeia out-ranges you badly with Noxious Blast — 850 to your 550 — and Serpentine Grace makes every move-speed buff kite your E flip harder. Avoid her poison: Twin Fang deals bonus damage to poisoned targets and heals her for a share of it. Never flip in with Miasma up; it grounds you and the E re-cast dies mid-air. Farm with Q from max range and wait for a Miasma gap.

notes: Fabricated 'Noxious Blight' removed from early and whys[1] and spikes[0]; real name is Noxious Blast. 'Petrify' replaced with Petrifying Gaze. Rows 0, 1, 2, 4 and 6 include no-op side edits so the group is complete; if the applier rejects identical before/after values, only the changed rows (2 content, 3, 5, 6 full) matter and they still leave both layers agreeing.
